caption: The drawing depicts a single ceramic vessel positioned centrally on a plain background. The vessel is ovular in shape, tapering at the bottom and curving outward towards a wide, circular opening at the top. The primary color of the vessel appears dark or charcoal, and it is adorned with decorative patterns. Around the upper section, a horizontal band features a repeated diamond and dot motif combined with a leaf-like design, bordered with dotted lines above and below. On the main body of the vessel, there is a large circular wreath pattern composed of leaf shapes arranged along the perimeter, forming a ring. The background consists of light beige or tan tones with uneven shading, and there are faint horizontal lines suggesting a surface or table beneath the vessel. The artwork uses a monochromatic palette, dominated by shades of gray, black, and tan. The medium appears to involve a combination of drawing and possibly wash or transfer, giving the image a slightly translucent and soft-edged appearance. To the right side of the vessel, near the bottom, there is a small vertical inscription with partially legible text.
title: Enameled Pewter Beaker
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
